subject: Rapid queue amplification causing p95/p99 regressions on Hosted API - BrightFields
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@brightfields.com>

Date: Fri, 14 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate (BrightFields production)

Jordan —

We started seeing a sharp increase in tail latency and a small uptick in 503s across our calls to /v1/generate around 08:45 PDT this morning. Key quick observations: 
- p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s, p99 to ~3.9s for a period of ~25 minutes.
- Error rate (5xx) rose to ~0.7% during the window.
- The spike correlates with a scheduled workflow run that fan-outs ~60 parallel requests per user session.

Attached is a short CSV excerpt from our side (BrightFields_latency_log_20280914.csv). Our product is user-facing and this caused a handful of support tickets. Can you confirm if this is on your end and what the mitigation plan is? We need an ETA and whether this is likely to reoccur in the next few hours.

Thanks,
Alice
Sr. Platform Engineer
BrightFields Inc.

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate (BrightFields production)

On Fri, Sep 14, 2028 at 09:29 AM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Initial ask: can the infra team confirm whether batching/queue depth increased for the hosted-api pool serving BrightFields and whether any kernel/quantization rollout touched those hosts in the 08:30–09:00 window?

Quick preliminary findings from the incident snapshot I pulled: 
- The batcher depth for routing tag brightfields-prod surged from a median of 6 to peaks of 48 for the 08:40–09:10 window.
- We saw sustained KV cache miss spikes for that pool — likely caused by many short-lived sessions that each had unique prompt prefixes (the fan-out pattern Alice mentioned).
- No model binary/quantization rollout was active in that pool during the window; there was a mesh-controller config change at 07:15 (non-runtime) unrelated to batching.

Likely root cause (quick hypothesis): the combination of heavy fanout per session + disabled prefix caching on BrightFields' integration caused the batcher to accumulate a large number of small but distinct requests. Batcher then amplified queue depth which increased per-request wait time and produced the observed p95/p99 regressions.

Short-term mitigations I recommend (can be executed within 10–25 mins):
1) Temporarily apply a per-customer concurrency cap at the router (~20 concurrent requests) to limit batcher growth.
2) Route BrightFields traffic to a larger dedicated pool we can spin up (adds capacity and isolates queueing impact).
3) Re-enable/advise on prefix/kv caching for their workflow to reduce distinct cache keys per session.

I’m standing by to run the cap and route change; will coordinate with infra for the pool spin-up.

—Stephanie
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Platform
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Sudden p95/p99 spikes on /v1/generate (BrightFields production)

We verified Stephanie’s snapshot. Actionables we can do now: 
- Apply a soft concurrency cap (router token bucket) for brightfields-prod to 20 concurrent requests — rolling change taking ~4 minutes to converge.
- Provision a temporary dedicated pool (2x current) and start warm-up; ETA ~18 minutes to accept traffic.
- Create an emergency route that pins BrightFields to the dedicated pool and enable immediate failover.

I’ll initiate the concurrency cap and pool spin up now. Rishi will handle the routing change and monitoring hooks to confirm p95 improvements.

Also: we should add an executive note and consider offering BrightFields a transient credit for the impacted window. Jordan — can you coordinate customer comms?

—Markus

Date: Fri, 15 Sep 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: Mitigation complete + follow-up plan (BrightFields)

Alice/Bob —

Thanks again for the quick heads-up yesterday. Here’s a summary of what we did and next steps: 
- Mitigation performed: router concurrency cap (20) applied at 10:36 PDT; temporary dedicated pool spun up and traffic routed at 10:54 PDT. Observed p95 drop from ~1.6s to ~260ms within three minutes of cutover; p99 similarly reduced.
- Root cause (engineering assessment): request amplification from BrightFields' parallel fan-out pattern plus high cardinality prompt prefixes prevented effective KV/prefix caching and allowed the batcher to accumulate many small distinct requests. That queue amplification increased wait-time and therefore p95/p99.
- Permanent recommendations: implement prefix caching for their workflow, add a regional dedicated routing policy for high-fanout customers, and add an adaptive concurrency control we can tune per-customer.

We’ve attached the incident action plan (queue-amplification_action_plan_v1.pdf) and the latency excerpt you sent. I’ve opened SUP-9821 for tracking and provided a Drive folder with logs and dashboards: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1Qz-queue-amp-BF-2028.

We’ll continue to monitor BrightFields closely over the next 48 hours. I’ll coordinate a short post-incident call to walk through the plan and timeline for prefix-caching changes. For now, apologies for the disruption — we’ll issue a credit for the impacted window; procurement (Bob) I’ll pull pricing/credit terms and follow up with your finance contact.

If you want an exec-level summary for your leadership, I can provide a one-pager this afternoon.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
